name: Hands on the Button: The Leaders of the Cold War
description: From Truman and Stalin to Reagan and Gorbachev: the leaders who steered two blocs through crises, proxy wars and an unexpectedly quiet end.

checkpoints.name: Two camps
checkpoints.note: Truman and Stalin, allies against Germany, became rivals, and Winston Churchill spoke of an iron curtain in 1946. The Marshall Plan, the Berlin Blockade and NATO split Europe. Mao Zedong won power in China in 1949, and Kim Il Sung's North Korea fought the Korean War.

checkpoints.name: Brinkmanship
checkpoints.note: After Stalin, Nikita Khrushchev led the Soviet side and Dwight Eisenhower the American, and the Warsaw Pact answered NATO. De Gaulle kept France apart, Nasser and Tito led non-aligned states, Castro took Cuba, and Kennedy and Khrushchev faced off in the Cuban Missile Crisis.

checkpoints.name: Hot wars, cold talks
checkpoints.note: Lyndon B. Johnson sent large forces to the Vietnam War, where Ho Chi Minh's North Vietnam fought on. Richard Nixon opened talks with Moscow and visited China in 1972, Jimmy Carter followed him, and after Mao's death Deng Xiaoping steered China toward economic reform.

checkpoints.name: The thaw and the end
checkpoints.note: Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan pressed the Western case, Pope John Paul II and Lech Walesa's Solidarity challenged communist rule in Poland, and Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms opened the way for change. Vaclav Havel became a leading voice, the Berlin Wall fell in 1989 and the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.
